summary: The change passes: it does what the retry asked. The planner prompt now requires a plan for any landing, history-check or attribution rule to include a table of every commit shape the real branch holds (job commits, records-only, owner-path, intervention, retry-after-block landing), with the rule's outcome for each. It also requires demonstrating the rule on a realistic-branch fixture and running the tests of every crate that calls the changed functions. The critic prompt now raises a major finding when any of these is missing. The CHANGELOG entry names the root cause, where the fix is, the three introspections, and that the guard is prose-only. The new budget lines (planner 1125, critic 974, both of 1300) match the computed counts. The new pinning test and all 121 athena-context tests pass, and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` passes too. I confirmed the new test would fail on the old prompts by reading them: none of the pinned phrases appear. I did not actually revert the files, because my role forbids changes. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. The frame-size bound went from 700 to 800, which was necessary and is as small as possible: the planner frame is now 799 tokens. No out-of-scope files changed, and the drain test is untouched. The only finding is a nit: that bound now leaves 1 token of room, so the next planner edit will have to raise it again.
